Colin Pearson had his work cut out to get in front of Leo Coy who is running better and better these days and particularly good runs came from Brian Gorman, closing in the Belgrave team in 60th place, and youngsters Simon Williamson and Pete Hardwick.
Pete Hardwick is progressing nicely these days and it surely will not be long before the more seasoned campaigners are struggling to hold this youngster back.

Revelation of the race was the running of Peter Hardwick. A year in athletics has seen him come on nicely; not the instant success of "here today and gone tomorrow" but the gradual, solid progress borne of hard graft.
Late news: Peter Hardwick - 1975/76 winner. A recent welcome visitor was Stan Davies, a good team man in his active days and a great club man.

Our scoring men, mostly "the old gang" were anchored by Steve Williams with Peter Hardwick and Simon Holmes hot on his heels - these three are soon going to worry our established seniors.

Of the other Belgravians David Searle pulled through over the later stages to claim the scalp of Peter Hardwick. Overall, however, the result was a poor one for Belgrave and the hoped for signs of a resurgance in distance running were not evident in this race.

Another two close together are Peter Hardwick 916th in 3:01.48 (Unigate) and John Wasbrough 927th in 3:02.09 (Goldenlay/Poly). In position 1054 our worthy handicapper, Arthur Bruce who clocked 3:09.01 and travelled all the way to New York to do it.

Paul Richley proved how promising he is with a good 30.24 and there were several p.b.'s from other of our improving runners particularly pleasing was Pete Hardwick's breakthrough and he duly won the handicap.

Chris Steer ran above expectations and Peter Hardwick confirmed that his 5¾ run was no fluke - Welcome to the 'A' team Pete! Laurie and Leo ran well but both admitted that the London Marathon of the previous week must have slowed them.

We recently received an e-mail from Pete Hardwick who ran for Belgrave Harriers from 1974 until he emigrated to America in 1981. He used to run primarily with Brian Gorman and Keith Duckett with training advice from Arthur Bruce.
